title: Native recipes, developer tooling, and a clearer desktop
summary: CloudlessOS 0.2.4 makes advanced inference recipes understandable and repeatable, adds first-class terminal and custom-engine workflows, improves multi-Spark preparation, and further refines the desktop around active AI work.
changes: Unify the active model and live metrics into one aligned desktop control while hiding unavailable metrics during model loading.
Keep the desktop shelf visible during AI startup and clearly dim pinned applications until the engine is ready.
Simplify the desktop shelf by removing its redundant label and move Places into a centered menu with a clear separator from pinned applications.
Present multi-Spark hardware as an aggregate summary with expandable per-device telemetry and clearer storage usage.
Align the Ask Cloudless control, active-model capsule, hardware, and desktop spacing into a more consistent responsive grid.
Adopt locally bundled Roboto and Roboto Mono typography and the official vector Cloudless wordmark across the desktop and first-launch experience.
Adapt hardware, model, app-install, download, update, driver, recipe, cluster, and welcome-tour progress bars to each appearance theme.
Simplify GitHub recipe prefilling with a fixed repository prefix, owner/repository input, and inline validation.
Expand Profile from a small hard-coded list to 68 alphabetized regions, including United Arab Emirates.
Synchronize single-timezone region choices such as United Arab Emirates with the host timezone and render the Cloudless clock explicitly in that timezone.
Prefer Ubuntu's active timezone link over stale legacy timezone metadata so Settings and the desktop clock remain accurate after a change.
Replace the experimental SparkRun dependency with Cloudless-native, pinned recipe manifests and lifecycle commands that remain inspectable and reproducible.

Prepare custom recipe runtimes and model caches once on the coordinator, then transfer the resulting runtime image and cache to peer Sparks over the direct cluster link instead of rebuilding or downloading twice.

Warn before a recipe needs a specialized inference runtime, explain why the standard Cloudless vLLM engine is insufficient, and show runtime size, cache state, cluster work, API routing, and every launch step.

Run recipe preparation as a daemon-owned background operation that remains visible and abortable after Model Manager is closed, with byte progress, percentage, estimated time remaining, and an eight-stage timeline.
Label coordinator-to-peer recipe transfers explicitly so users can see which Spark is downloading, preparing, or receiving runtime and model data.
Add an unrestricted floating terminal with up to eight persistent tabs, plus optional developer tooling for CUDA, source builds, and architecture-specific experimentation.
Introduce a managed custom-engine registry so locally compiled vLLM and SGLang images can be selected as first-class engines without replacing the signed system engine.

Separate the locked private inference runtime from the client API identity, allowing users to change the authenticated API port and model alias without letting recipes or custom engines break Hermes and application routing.
Remove the dormant public recipe indexer and discovery UI while retaining local recipe import, editing, checking, and execution.
